deep_dive.title: Predicting Quantization Price for Selecting PTQ Configurations Before Deployment
deep_dive.abstract: Weight-space post-training quantization (PTQ) must choose finite formats, granularities, quantizer families, transformations, and bits before the completed quantized model reveals its output-distribution drift. Existing PTQ methods predict important pieces of this degradation, including reconstruction error, Hessian sensitivity, transformation effects, and downstream loss, but these pieces are usually scored after fixing the quantization geometry or inside separate configuration families. We formulate weight-space PTQ as pre-deployment configuration selection using priced layer-output error. Each admissible layer configuration is treated as an error generator with a deployment cost, which induces a layer-output error covariance $\boldsymbolΣ_l(α_l)$, and the full-precision model prices that covariance by downstream curvature, $\widehatρ_l(α_l)=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{Tr}\left(\widehat{\mathbf{H}}_l\,\widehat{\boldsymbolΣ}_l(α_l)\right)$. The price follows from full-precision-to-quantized forward KL, whose first-order term cancels at the reference model. It turns reconstruction and diagonal scores into reduced proxies that drop price factors, while finite formats, codebooks, granularities, and equivalent transformations become comparable candidates through the covariances they induce and the costs they pay. A trace reduction then yields a calibration-time price table and a budgeted price-guided selector, making fixed-geometry bit allocation a special case rather than the organizing problem.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: Weight-space PTQ must pick formats, granularities, transformations and bits before drift is observable; this paper casts PTQ as pre-deployment configuration selection, treating each layer configuration as a priced error generator with an induced output error covariance.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 权重后训练量化需在部署前确定格式、粒度、量化器族、变换与比特数，而现有方法多在固定量化几何后分别评估重建误差、Hessian敏感度等指标。本文将权重PTQ形式化为部署前的配置选择问题，把每种层配置视为带部署代价的误差生成器，导出层输出误差协方差。实验表明该代价预测能更统一地比较不同配置族，从而在部署前选出更优的量化方案。

quick_skim.title: Text Scores Can Miss Waveform Use: A Qwen2-Audio Quantization Case Study
quick_skim.abstract: Post-training quantization of speech language models is often summarized with text-output scores and nominal bit widths. Those numbers alone do not establish behavior that depends on information missing from a transcript, or efficiency for a particular runtime. We introduce an evaluation protocol that separately tests lexical output, a transcript-insufficient endpoint, and a measured packed implementation. In a Qwen2-Audio case study, a translation-selected 6-bit allocation improves chrF by 2.36 on a frozen English-to-German replay, with paired 95% bootstrap interval [1.04, 3.62], but loses 3.91 percentage points on speaker-disjoint emotion recognition. At the same 6-bit budget, the uniform structural control reaches higher emotion accuracy than the selected allocation, and the front-layer control is also higher by point estimate on the same frozen set. At 7 bits, chrF improves by 3.28 with interval [2.08, 4.59], the emotion interval against FP16 includes zero, and a same-budget front-layer control still exceeds the selected allocation. A separate matched-budget 4.08-bit study finds roughly 10-point emotion deficits for every tested low-bit allocation and no selected-allocation advantage over frozen controls. Finally, a dequantized average-6-bit simulation retains the FP16 peak memory. This case study identifies a precision-dependent mismatch between lexical output, waveform-dependent behavior, and nominal precision. It does not establish a general failure of low-bit speech models or a deployment benefit for the selected allocation.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: quantization sensitivity across lexical text output versus waveform-dependent tasks

quick_skim.title: Compressing Long Context into Answer-Aligned Memory Embeddings for LLM Inference
quick_skim.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference is constrained by the quadratic scaling of self-attention and the linear scaling of the KV cache, increasing latency, energy consumption, and GPU memory demand as context length scales. Existing soft-compression methods either lack query-guided memory selection at inference time, train without answer-targeted supervision, or couple compression tightly to a specific decoder architecture. We propose a Context-to-Answer-Aligned Memory Compression (CMC) framework, which compresses long input contexts into compact Context Memory Embeddings (CMEs) aligned to any frozen decoder's embedding space, reducing inference costs without modifying decoder weights. CMC introduces a two-tier KV cache that combines question-guided CME selection with a local context window, and trains the compressor with answer-targeted distillation from a frozen LLM. Experiments across nine encoder-decoder combinations and four QA benchmarks show that CMC consistently outperforms the baseline, achieving up to 7.3 EM and 4.0 F1 point gains on SQuAD, while reducing inference time and energy consumption by up to 20% and peak reserved GPU memory by up to 50% at 3,000 generation tokens. Ablation studies confirm that each architectural component and training objective contributes to the performance.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对LLM推理中自注意力二次开销与KV缓存线性增长带来的延迟与显存压力，以及现有软压缩方法缺乏查询引导、答案监督或与解码器耦合过紧的问题，作者提出CMC框架，将长输入上下文压缩为对齐任意冻结解码器嵌入空间的上下文记忆嵌入，并设计两级KV缓存。该方法无需修改解码器权重即可降低推理成本，同时通过答案对齐监督提升压缩记忆的可用性，为长上下文LLM推理高效化提供了可行路径。

quick_skim.matched_query_text: Papers central to 围绕 LLM/VLM 高效压缩与适配的研究检索关键词, especially work that connects or combines: post-training quantization techniques for large language models including GPTQ AWQ SmoothQuant and OmniQuant; joint quantization and low-rank adaptation for memory efficient fine-tuning of large models; applying orthogonal rotation or Hadamard transforms to reduce outlier effects in weight quantization; reducing the number of visual tokens in vision language models through pruning and merging; compressing video tokens while preserving temporal grounding and event detection; quantization sensitivity of visual and textual modalities in vision language models; How does orthogonal rotation affect the low rank structure of quantization error in large language models?; Can low rank adapters reconstruct quantization error after rotation better than before rotation?; What is the interaction between visual token pruning and post training quantization in vision language models?; How can we preserve temporal information when merging video tokens for video understanding models?.
